questions.stem: A body starts from rest and moves with a uniform acceleration of 2 m s^-2. The distance covered in the first 5 s is
The area under a velocity-time graph gives
questions.explanation: Integrating velocity with respect to time gives displacement.

questions.stem: A ball is thrown vertically upwards with 20 m s^-1. Taking g = 10 m s^-2, the maximum height reached is
Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
questions.explanation: Distance has magnitude only; the rest are vectors.

questions.stem: A car covers the first half of a distance at 30 km h^-1 and the second half at 60 km h^-1. Its average speed for the whole journey is
questions.explanation: For equal distances, average speed = 2v1v2/(v1+v2) = 2(30)(60)/90 = 40 km h^-1.

questions.stem: For a body moving with constant velocity, the displacement-time graph is
options: A straight line inclined to the time axis
A straight line parallel to the time axis
questions.explanation: Constant velocity means displacement changes uniformly with time, giving a sloped straight line.

questions.stem: Newton's second law of motion is best expressed as
questions.explanation: Force equals the rate of change of linear momentum.

questions.stem: A force of 10 N acts on a body of mass 2 kg. The acceleration produced is
Impulse of a force is equal to the change in
questions.explanation: Impulse = F.dt = change in momentum.

questions.stem: Rocket propulsion is based on the principle of conservation of
questions.explanation: Exhaust gases carry momentum backwards, so the rocket gains equal forward momentum.

questions.stem: A 5 kg block rests on a rough horizontal surface with coefficient of friction 0.2 (g = 10 m s^-2). The limiting friction is
Action and reaction forces described by Newton's third law
questions.explanation: They act on two different bodies, so they never cancel on a single body.

questions.stem: The work done by the centripetal force on a body in uniform circular motion is
questions.explanation: The force is perpendicular to displacement at every instant, so W = 0.

questions.stem: The kinetic energy of a 2 kg body moving with 3 m s^-1 is
According to the work-energy theorem, the net work done on a body equals the change in its
questions.explanation: W_net = KE_final - KE_initial.

questions.stem: One watt is equal to
questions.explanation: Power is work per unit time, so 1 W = 1 J s^-1.

questions.stem: A body of mass 1 kg is raised through a height of 10 m (g = 10 m s^-2). The gain in potential energy is
questions.explanation: PE = mgh = 1 x 10 x 10 = 100 J.

questions.stem: In a perfectly inelastic collision, which quantity is always conserved?
questions.explanation: Momentum is conserved in all collisions; kinetic energy is lost in inelastic ones.

questions.stem: The SI unit of electrical resistivity is
questions.explanation: rho = RA/l, so the unit is ohm metre.

questions.stem: Two resistors of 4 ohm each are connected in parallel. The equivalent resistance is
The relation between current and drift velocity is
questions.explanation: Current equals charge density times electron charge times area times drift velocity.

questions.stem: Kirchhoff's junction rule is a consequence of conservation of
questions.explanation: Total charge entering a junction equals the charge leaving it.

questions.stem: A wire of resistance R is stretched to double its length keeping the volume constant. Its new resistance is
questions.explanation: Length doubles and area halves, so R' = rho(2l)/(A/2) = 4R.

questions.stem: A potentiometer measures the emf of a cell accurately because at the balance point
options: Maximum current flows through the cell
No current is drawn from the cell
questions.explanation: At null deflection no current flows, so there is no internal resistance drop.

questions.stem: The focal length of a plane mirror is
options: Equal to half the object distance
questions.explanation: A plane mirror has an infinite radius of curvature, so f = R/2 is infinite.

questions.stem: For a medium of refractive index 1.5, the critical angle with respect to air is approximately
questions.explanation: sin C = 1/n = 0.667, so C is about 41.8 degrees.

questions.stem: The power of a convex lens of focal length 20 cm is
questions.explanation: P = 1/f (in metres) = 1/0.2 = 5 D.

questions.stem: Total internal reflection can occur when light travels from
options: A rarer to a denser medium
A denser to a rarer medium
One medium to another of equal refractive index
questions.explanation: It requires the angle of incidence in the denser medium to exceed the critical angle.

questions.stem: The image formed by a convex mirror of a real object is always
questions.explanation: A convex mirror always forms a virtual, erect and smaller image.
